answer: The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, slashed on a failed audit. Reaching the umber of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Every claim climbs the karst of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the spiral re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short.
